method: Stratified random sample: rows of person-wikidata.jsonl filtered by tier in file order; one random.Random(20261011) generator; rng.sample(pool,15) per tier in the order title_verified, probable_historian, probable_canadian_academic, possible_sole_candidate. Cited works: AUTHORED edges from the graph.json Person node, sorted by Work cited_by_all desc, top 5. Two sampled row keys (P:fecteau|jean, P:dummitt|chris) are absent from graph.json; they were resolved to the graph node carrying the same QID (P:fecteau|jeanmarie, P:dummitt|christopher). Across the whole file, 75 of 4030 rows have this key drift. Wikidata evidence: QLever (qlever.dev/api/wikidata) batched queries for label, description, P31, P106, P569/P570, P108, P69, P101, P27, P800, inverse P50, and VIAF/ORCID/ISNI; full direct statements for thin items; label lookups for alternative items; at least 2 s between requests. For thin items, the authority records linked from the Wikidata item were checked: id.loc.gov MARC 670 source citations, and GND via lobid.org. No Wikidata REST search was used. Verdict: correct = QID is the person who wrote the dominant cited works; wrong = a different person; unsure = insufficient evidence. Where historiographical knowledge was used, the evidence says so.
